probe: zpool is installed and `zpool status -j` answers; a host carrying zpool with no imported pool still answers, and that is a reading of zero pools rather than a probe failure

collections.name: pools
collections.question: are my pools healthy, what does each one survive losing, and when was one last scrubbed?

guid.sentence: The pool GUID, which survives rename and import. Carried as a decimal STRING because it is a full unsigned 64-bit value: routed through a float or a signed integer it comes back as a different pool, and a join key that changes value in transit is not a key.

devices.sentence: Every disk member, named as `zpool status` keys it — a by-id link on most hosts, a bare kernel name on a pool imported as one. Group members (log, cache, spare) are included: they are devices this pool holds open.

kernel.sentence: The kernel device paths those members resolve to today, through the device alias trees. Reassigned on rescan; carried because a person searches for /dev/sdc, and joined on never.

State.sentence: The pool's overall verdict, in ZFS's own word for it — ONLINE, DEGRADED, FAULTED, SUSPENDED. Passed through exactly as the document spells it rather than mapped onto a set this reading would have to keep closed.

StatusMessage.sentence: The catalogue prose zpool prints when something is wrong, trimmed of surrounding whitespace and otherwise verbatim. A healthy pool has none, and says so through the absent list.

Errors.sentence: Known DATA errors: blocks ZFS could not reconstruct. Zero beside a non-zero member counter means parity repaired every bad block, so this and the per-vdev counters answer different questions and neither substitutes for the other.

ScanFunction.sentence: What kind of scan the pool's single scan record describes — SCRUB or RESILVER. ZFS keeps only the most recent, so a resilver replaces the scrub's record entirely.

ScanState.sentence: Where that scan stands: SCANNING while in progress, FINISHED when complete. A scan in progress has no end time yet, which is why ScanEndTime and ScanAgeDays are absent mid-scrub.

ScanEndTime.sentence: When the recorded scan finished, in UTC to the second. On the absent list while a scan is running, because an end time of zero means it has not ended and not the epoch; on an OpenZFS too old to render epochs it is the prose date verbatim, and then no age is derived from it.

ScanAgeDays.sentence: Whole days since the recorded scan finished — the SCAN, not necessarily the scrub: after a resilver this counts from the resilver, which is what LastScrubEndTime exists to say out loud.

LastScrubEndTime.sentence: When the last completed SCRUB finished. ZFS keeps one scan record, so where a later resilver overwrote it this fact is an unobservable record rather than a value — the time exists and this pool cannot report it.

LastScrubEndTimeUnobservable.sentence: Why the last scrub's end time cannot be read from this pool. Present only in that state, so a stale-scrub rule can cite the stated unknown instead of going silent beside a months-old scrub.

SizeBytes.sentence: Total raw capacity, before parity and before compression.

AllocatedBytes.sentence: Raw bytes ZFS has allocated, parity included.

FreeBytes.sentence: Raw bytes unallocated. Not a promise about how much a dataset can still be written, which parity and compression both move.

CapacityPercent.sentence: Allocated over size, as whole percent, exactly as ZFS reports it rather than recomputed here.

FragmentationPercent.sentence: ZFS's own whole-percent measure of free-space fragmentation. Deliberately carries no unit: it is not a fraction of any figure published here, and declaring it a percentage would demand a denominator that does not exist.

Vdevs.sentence: The vdev tree flattened to one row per device, in the order zpool reports it, each row carrying its depth, type, state, error counters, its own stable names, and — where the alias trees resolved it — the kernel block device it is. A row whose Device could not be resolved because no alias tree was readable says so on its own unobservable record, at Vdevs/<name>/Device.

UnhealthyVdevs.sentence: Every member whose state is neither ONLINE nor AVAIL, groups included, in tree order. A spare sitting AVAIL is standing by and protecting nothing yet, which is not a fault; a member that reported no state at all made no statement to disagree with.

VdevsWithErrors.sentence: Every member carrying a non-zero read, write or checksum counter, in tree order. Membership overlaps UnhealthyVdevs only by coincidence: a member can be OFFLINE with no errors, or ONLINE having had every bad block repaired.

Redundancy.sentence: How this pool's data vdevs are laid out, in zpool's own words — stripe, mirror, raidz1. A pool is only as redundant as its weakest data vdev, because losing any one of them loses the pool, so a mixed layout is named in full ("raidz1 + stripe") rather than summarised to its best part. Where the walk meets a top-level shape it cannot read it claims nothing at all, on the unobservable channel.

DeviceFailuresTolerated.sentence: How many whole devices this pool survives losing, read from the layout above; 0 means the next disk to fail takes the pool with it. Stated and graded by nothing here — whether that is a problem depends on what lives on the pool, which this reading cannot see.

VdevPath.sentence: The vdev this member sits directly inside, as zpool names it — a raidz or mirror group, the spare-N pseudo-vdev a replacement creates, the group key a log, cache or spare arrived under, or the pool's own root vdev for a stripe member. It is the discriminator because an engaged spare is genuinely two members of one pool at once: standing in `spares` and working inside spare-N.

collections.redaction_exemption: zpool status and zpool list have no credential surface: every member is a device name, a state word, a counter, a capacity figure or a scan statistic. The identifiers this collection publishes verbatim — pool guid, vdev names, devid and wwn — are the join keys it exists to provide, and each is declared as disclosing identity on its own fact rather than withheld from the evidence that proves it was read.

reference_commands.purpose: the alias trees Device resolves through
